title: Use Albania MTPL as the learning ground for the next launch
recommendation: Improve and measure the existing MyIute motor journey before treating it as the template for another product or market.

whyNow.text: Compulsory insurance represented 62.38% of Albanian premiums in 2025, and domestic MTPL contracts grew 6.85%.
From 2026, MTPL pricing uses bonus-malus and seven risk factors. The regulator requires electronic premium calculators.
MyIute already offers plate-led pricing, four instalments at no added cost, in-app policy access and a SIGAL claims handoff.

hypothesis: Convenience is already visible. The next advantage may come from trusted cover status, renewal relevance and clear service ownership.
assumptions: Payment flexibility creates incremental adoption or persistency, not only channel substitution.
Digital proof is trusted, while paper and human-help needs are handled without breaking the journey.
Carrier service, claims and exception economics remain healthy as volume grows.

plan.title: Baseline the journey
plan.detail: Funnel, issuance, proof access, service reasons, claims handoffs, renewal and contribution by cohort.

plan.title: Explain the breaks
plan.detail: Interview buyers, abandoners and renewers. Review service, complaint and failed-issuance cases with operations.

plan.title: Test the wedge
plan.detail: Prototype cover verification, renewal timing and ownership messages. Test comprehension before changing the full journey.

plan.title: Make the decision
plan.detail: Review customer, Iute and carrier evidence together. Proceed, change the proposition or stop.

gates.title: The trust-and-renewal wedge holds
gates.evidence: Better qualified completion or renewal, with stable complaints, exceptions, cost to serve and carrier service.

gates.title: Demand exists but the service breaks
gates.evidence: Fix proof, support or partner handoffs before adding reach, cover or another market.

gates.title: No incremental value or controllable economics
gates.evidence: Do not scale if demand is substitution, contribution is weak, or partner and control risks remain unresolved.

alternatives.name: MyIute + SIGAL
alternatives.observed: Plate-led pricing, four instalments, policy in app, renewal reminder and insurer-owned claims handling.
alternatives.reading: Convenience and financing are real. The next test is whether Iute can make status, renewal and service ownership more trusted.

alternatives.name: SIGAL + ALBSIG
alternatives.observed: Public journeys already support online motor purchase or calculation. SIGAL also offers related motor and roadside products online.
alternatives.reading: Digital purchase alone is not a defensible difference. Relevance, payment, proof and lifecycle service must earn the choice.

alternatives.name: Branches + agents
alternatives.observed: EUROSIG describes 33 branches, more than 230 agencies and points of sale, and an original policy copy for the customer.
alternatives.reading: Physical reach and paper proof are established alternatives. A digital route must preserve confidence and access to help.

alternatives.name: AFSA policy registry
alternatives.observed: Customers can verify current compulsory motor cover through the regulator's online registry or by SMS.
alternatives.reading: Verification is part of the experience. Surface it at the moment of doubt instead of expecting customers to find it.

changeMyMind: Another customer problem has materially higher unmet need and better three-sided economics.
Current MTPL performance shows trust and renewal are already strong, with no material service friction.
Carrier, regulatory or platform constraints make this a poor learning ground for reusable capability.
